Package hadur2.core.move

Class EscapeRoom

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.move.EscapeRoom
public final class EscapeRoom extends Object
MOVE-12: how much of its escape angle a robot keeps inside the field.

A bullet of speed v fired from source at a robot at target can be escaped, at speed 8, to exactly the points P where |PT| / 8 <= |PS| / v: the disc of an Apollonius circle (diameter from 8d/(v+8) short of the target to 8d/(v-8) beyond it, d the distance). The widest angle the target can get from the source's line of fire on either side is where that disc, cut to the area a robot's centre can occupy, is widest as seen from the source. That is the exact "precise positional" escape angle, found in constant time (no sampling) among the candidates: the tangent points from the source (when they lie in the field), where the circle crosses the four walls, and the field's corners inside the circle.

The restriction is the in-field escape angles summed over twice the open-field one (asin(8/v)): 1 in the open, falling toward 0 as walls take that side's room away. Each side is floored at 0.001 rad so the ratio never divides by zero. Cost: four line/circle solves, four corner tests and one small array, three or four times per surf option.

      public static double multiplier(Point2D.Double ourEnd, Point2D.Double enemy, double bulletSpeed, BattleField field)
      The position term: restriction(ourEnd, enemy) over restriction(enemy, ourEnd) squared. Above 1 when the enemy has room to escape our bullets from where we end, below 1 when we have room to escape his; a danger multiplied by it prefers ends that keep our escape angle and cost him his.
      Parameters:
      ourEnd - where we would be when the wave passes, in px
      enemy - the wave's source, in px
      bulletSpeed - the wave's bullet speed, in px per tick
      field - the field
      Returns:
      the factor, above 0
